results.summary_before: This is a numerically controlled oscillator that produces an unsigned 8-bit waveform selected by two mode pins: sine from a lookup table, or square and sawtooth from the phase accumulator. The design is small and the documentation covers the pin protocol but not the output sample rate or table depth.
results.summary: This design samples an input bit and evaluates whether the bit source is random using the Monobit test from NIST 800.22. It produces an is_random output that is valid only when the valid signal is high. The result is updated every 65536 cycles. The design is written in Verilog and currently requires no external hardware.

The design includes D flip-flop debouncing logic and slow clock enables for the button inputs. The PWM output can be used to control LEDs or other devices. Control and status are exchanged over an SCI interface that requires synchronization. The design is written in Verilog and includes debug outputs.

It is a digital division circuit that computes the quotient and remainder of binary numbers. The design is purely combinational and does not require a clock. results.summary: This design is an example of a bad synchronizer based on Figure 29.3 from Dally & Harting. It exposes stage1, stage2, and stage3 signals along with a skew output for observing bit errors. Testing involves aligning and then separating the clocks to look for errors. The design is written in Verilog and requires an external clock source.

results.summary: This design is an 8-bit signed/unsigned multiply and divide unit. It uses latches to capture two 8-bit inputs through a multiplexed interface and provides immediate or registered results. The divider reports overflow and divide-by-zero errors, while multiplier mode mutes error bits. The design is written in SpinalHDL and can be tested with an RP2040 and Python REPL.

results.summary: This project implements a 4-bit ALU that performs arithmetic and logical operations on two 4-bit inputs selected by a 4-bit opcode. It outputs an 8-bit result along with carry-out and overflow status. The design is written in Verilog and can be tested by cycling through opcode values and observing the outputs. The documentation includes a test procedure using the input and output pins.
